record.paper_title: Modal logics for metric spaces: open problems
record.original_question: For full QMS, the metric modal language with quantified distance variables and the MS distance operators, characterize which fragments are decidable and which are undecidable over natural classes of distance or metric models.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix a countable set of propositional variables and a countable set of positive-real-valued distance variables. The modal language QMS is built over a variable-free modal base MS whose primitive operators are, for each rational a > 0, parameterized distance modalities ∃^{<a} φ ("there is a point at distance less than a satisfying φ") and ∃^{≤a} φ, together with their duals; QMS extends MS by allowing the rational parameter a to be replaced by a quantified distance variable x, with explicit quantifiers ∀x and ∃x ranging over positive reals (so that, e.g., ∀x ∃^{<x} φ is a well-formed formula).

A distance model is a pair (W, d) where d : W × W → [0, ∞] is a distance function, together with a valuation of propositional variables. A metric model is a distance model in which d is a metric (symmetric, satisfies the triangle inequality, and d(x, y) = 0 iff x = y). Standard natural subclasses include: all distance spaces, distance spaces satisfying the triangle inequality, all metric spaces, and the metric spaces ℝ^n, ℚ^n, ℤ^n with Euclidean distance (and their finite subspaces).

Problem. Give a systematic characterization of which syntactic fragments of full QMS (defined by restrictions on the use of distance quantifiers, on the alternation of distance and propositional modalities, on the number of distance variables, on Boolean combinations, etc.) have a decidable satisfiability/validity problem, and which are undecidable, over each of the natural classes of distance and metric models listed above.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of delimiting decidable versus undecidable fragments of the quantified metric modal language QMS is posed as an open program. Surveys and notes on logics of metric spaces (Kutz; Sheremet–Tishkovsky–Wolter–Zakharyaschev) describe partial results — for instance the variable-free MS is decidable over many classes and equi-expressive with the two-variable FM fragment, while certain quantitative extensions are undecidable over ℝ, ℚ, ℤ — but no general classification for full QMS appears to be available, so the problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Notes on Logics of Metric Spaces (O. Kutz)
status_evidence.snippet: One main problem is to delimit the borders between 'decidable' and 'undecidable' for these logics; some fragments are decidable while quantitative extensions interpreted over ℝ, ℚ, ℤ are undecidable.
status_evidence.claim: The decidability landscape of QMS-style logics is only partially understood.

status_evidence.title: From topology to metric: Modal logic and quantification in metric spaces
status_evidence.snippet: The two-variable fragment of FM is undecidable over metric spaces, while MS and natural fragments are decidable in various distance classes.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial decidability/undecidability results are known, leaving a full classification of QMS fragments open.
